This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

# Team Documentation Workflow

Collaboration centered on the `docs/` directory.

## Knowledge Architecture (domain-axis)

Docs are organized by what they're *about*, not by lifecycle stage. A doc's freshness lives in its TL;DR (and `Last touched:` for active areas) — not by which directory it sits in. Completed work stays co-located with its domain. There is no `archives/` directory — if a doc no longer earns its keep, delete it; if a lasting lesson hides inside it, lift that lesson into `lessons/` first, then delete.

```
docs/
├── index.md           # Routing table — every doc must be listed here
├── roadmap/           # Strategic plans, quarterly direction, milestones
├── models/<line>/     # Per-model living docs (qwen3, qwen35, kimi-k2, ...)
│                      # — design, accuracy, perf, refactor records, gotchas
├── subsystems/<area>/ # Cross-cutting components (runtime, scheduler, frontend, kernels)
├── playbooks/         # Reusable how-to: benching, profiling, accuracy, onboarding
├── lessons/           # Tribal knowledge from research / other projects
├── benchmarks/        # Standalone benchmark snapshots and eval reports
├── conventions/       # Ongoing standards (bench regression, coding style)
└── private/           # Local-only notes (gitignored)
```

Classification rule at capture time:
- Is it tied to a specific model? → `models/<line>/`
- A specific subsystem? → `subsystems/<area>/`
- Reusable how-to applicable across models? → `playbooks/`
- Lasting lesson from elsewhere (other repo, research, postmortem)? → `lessons/`
- Snapshot of measurement, not a doc that evolves? → `benchmarks/`
- Strategic / cross-cutting plan? → `roadmap/`

If you can't pick one, the doc probably needs splitting.

## Documentation Style

- Docs cover what `--help` and code can't: pitfalls, diagnostic paths, decision context. Don't restate CLI reference.
- Every command in a doc must be run and verified before committing. Unverified commands are technical debt.
- The only required header is a one-line **TL;DR**. Keep it true; that's the contract.
- For `models/<line>/` and `subsystems/<area>/` docs, add `Last touched: YYYY-MM` and bump it when you do meaningful work on the doc (not for typo fixes). The date is a fact, not a judgement — readers infer freshness themselves.
- `playbooks/`, `lessons/`, `conventions/`, `roadmap/`, `benchmarks/`, `archives/` don't need a freshness stamp. They're either timeless until disproven, or self-dated, or explicitly inert.
- No `Status:` enum. Enum fields go stale exactly when you need them most.

## index.md Drift Policy

`index.md` is a routing table with a scanning-friendly TL;DR column. It is *allowed to drift* from the TL;DR inside each doc — the doc body is authoritative. Update `index.md` when you create or delete a doc, or when the existing TL;DR is so wrong it actively misleads. Don't churn it on every doc edit.

## Core Principles (CODE)

Documentation exists to advance work, not to hoard information. Four steps when handling information:

1. **Capture**: Only record what materially advances the project. When in doubt, leave it out.
2. **Organize**: Action-oriented. Resist the urge to organize for organization's sake — structure should be just enough.
3. **Distill**: Refactor over append. When you learn something new or hit a pitfall, integrate it into the document body — don't pile a changelog at the bottom.
4. **Express**: Every document must point to a next step. Split unwieldy documents proactively. Active documents must note the current blocker or next action.

**Sync**

At the start of each session, you must read `index.md` and load the documents needed for the task at hand.

**Execute**
- Update relevant documents as you go. When a new problem or idea arises, create a document in the appropriate domain directory (see classification rule above).

**Commit**

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	# 消费方集成：kernels 与 cupti 如何使用 CudaToolkit
2	
3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	前几讲我们一直在读 `pegainfer-build` 这个库本身：discover 的回落链、target_dirs 的架构目录、from_root 的三种布局、existing_deduped 的收敛、header_dir 与 link_search 的输出。本讲换到**消费方视角**，回答一个新问题：**一个真实的 build.rs 拿到 `CudaToolkit` 之后，到底怎么用它的各个出口？**
6	
7	学完本讲你应该能够：
8	
9	1. 在 `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` 近三千行代码中定位**全部**工具包使用点，并逐个说明用途。
10	2. 说清 `header_dir("cuda.h")` 返回 `None` 时 kernels 的兜底路径（`toolkit.root.join("include")`），以及这个兜底在 conda 布局下为什么不可靠。
11	3. 对比两个消费方的使用深度：kernels 用 nvcc / header_dir / link_search / root 四个出口，而 cupti 不用 nvcc、却额外用 `root` 拼 `extras/CUPTI` 特例目录。
12	4. 独立画出「discover 输出 → 各消费点用途 → 最终 cargo: 指令（或编译器 argv）」的完整数据流图。
13	
14	## 2. 前置知识
15	
16	本讲假设你已完成 u1（build script 协议、lib.rs 导览）和 u2（探测机制精读）。在此之上补充四个新概念：
17	
18	- **宿主编译器 vs nvcc**：nvcc 编译 `.cu` 时自己知道 CUDA 工具包（CTK）的头文件在哪；但宿主机的 `cc` / `c++` 编译一个 `#include <cuda_runtime.h>` 的 C 包装文件时**不会**自动找到 CUDA 头，必须显式传 `-I`。这是 `header_dir` 存在的根本原因——它要回答「哪一个目录里**真的**有这个头文件」。
19	- **`-I` 与 `-isystem` 的区别**：两者都添加头文件搜索目录，但 `-isystem` 把目录标记为「系统头」（抑制其中警告），且优先级低于 `-I`。kernels 正是利用这个优先级差，把 CTK 头目录装进 `-isystem`、把自带的较新 CCCL 装进 `-I`，让后者覆盖前者。
20	- **cc crate**：Rust 生态驱动宿主 C/C++ 编译器的标准 build-dependency；`cc::Build::include(path)` 等价于给编译器加 `-I path`。
21	- **CUPTI**（CUDA Profiling Tools Interface）：CUDA 的性能剖析接口。它的头和库在经典安装里**不在**主 `include/`、`lib64/` 下，而在 `extras/CUPTI/` 子树——这是本讲第二个模块的主角。
22	
23	## 3. 本讲源码地图
24	
25	| 文件 | 体量 | 本讲角色 |
26	|---|---|---|
27	| `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` | 约 2930 行 | 构建总管：编译全部 CUDA 源、Triton AOT、TileLang、cutedsl，是 `CudaToolkit` 最重的消费方 |
28	| `pegainfer-cupti/build.rs` | 34 行 | 最小完整消费方：discover → include → compile → link 一条龙，外加 extras/CUPTI 特例 |
29	| `pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs` | 299 行 | 被消费的库本尊（u1-l3、u2 各讲已精读，本讲只引用关键行） |

31	
32	两个消费方在各自 `Cargo.toml` 的 `[build-dependencies]` 里以 workspace 依赖声明引用本库：[pegainfer-cupti/Cargo.toml:L7-L9](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/Cargo.toml#L7-L9)（`cc` + `pegainfer-build`）与 [pegainfer-kernels/Cargo.toml:L27-L29](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/Cargo.toml#L27-L29)（同样两条）。
33	
34	> **行号校准记录（update）**：上一版讲义以 223206b7 为基准。当前 HEAD 8886aa47 期间，73d998ea（Qwen4 分组 RMSNorm）与 8b5b84a9（DFlash2）触碰了 kernels，但 `build.rs` 只有 4 行改动：往 CCCL `-I` 门控清单加了两个 stem（[L2500](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2500) 的 `dflash2_selector`、[L2504](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2504) 的 `qwen4_grouped_rmsnorm`）并改写了一句 Qwen4 警告文案（[L2739](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2739)）。这使 L2500 以下行号整体 +2：尾部工具包出口从旧版的 2884-2887 漂移到 2886-2889；而 L929、L2209-2213 等锚点不变。`pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs` 与 `pegainfer-cupti/build.rs` 两个文件无任何改动。
35	
36	## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解
37	
38	### 4.1 kernels 构建链路中的工具包消费点
39	
40	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
41	
42	`pegainfer-kernels` 是整个工作区的构建总管：`csrc/*.cu` 的 nvcc 编译、qwen35 的 Triton AOT、glm52 的 TileLang 与 cutedsl 代码生成、静态库打包、kernel-lab 共享库链接，全部从这里发起。它对 `CudaToolkit` 的需求最全面：
43	
44	- 要一个**可执行的 nvcc 命令**（几十个并行编译任务都要用它）；
45	- 要一个**真正含 `cuda.h` 的头目录**，同时喂给 nvcc（`-isystem`）和宿主 cc（`-I`）；
46	- 要**库搜索路径**，在构建末尾变成 `cargo:rustc-link-search`。
47	
48	值得注意的是：kernels **从不直接遍历 `toolkit.include_dirs`**——它只消费 `header_dir("cuda.h")` 的单点结果。原因在 u2-l4 讲过：`include_dirs` 里可能有「存在却缺 CUDA 头」的目录（conda 前缀的 `include/`），只有按具体头文件探测才可靠。
49	
50	#### 4.1.2 核心流程
51	
52	kernels 的 `main()` 在开头一次性完成探测，之后所有消费点都用这三样派生物：
53	
54	```text
55	toolkit = CudaToolkit::discover()                    # L2209，全文件唯一探测点
56	nvcc         = toolkit.nvcc（转成字符串）             # L2210 → nvcc_command 包装 → 并行 worker 克隆
57	cuda_include = header_dir("cuda.h")                  # L2211-2212
58	               ?? toolkit.root.join("include")       # L2213，兜底（见 4.3.4）
59	
60	cuda_include 的四条下游：
61	  ├─ nvcc 编译 .cu        ：-isystem {cuda_include}          # L2353-2354
62	  ├─ glm52 cutedsl shim   ：宿主 cc -I                      # L2229 → L129
63	  ├─ qwen35 Triton AOT    ：断言 + 宿主 cc -I                # L2875 → L1323-1327 / L1506
64	  └─ TileLang 生成体      ：nvcc -I                          # L2748/2757/2771 → L2178-2179
65	
66	toolkit.root 的两条下游：
67	  ├─ kernel-lab .so 链接  ：-L {root}/lib64（仅 PEGAINFER_KERNEL_LAB）# L2871 → L944
68	  └─ Windows 库目录       ：cargo:rustc-link-search={root}/lib/x64    # L2883-2887
69	
70	lib_dirs 的唯一下游：
71	  └─ toolkit.link_search()（非 Windows）                    # L2889
72	       → cargo:rustc-link-search=native=... 配合 L2891-2899 的 link-lib 清单
73	```
74	
75	关键认知：`nvcc` 和 `cuda_include` 变成**子进程 argv**，`link_search` 变成 **cargo: 指令**——`CudaToolkit` 的出口一半喂编译器、一半喂 Cargo，两类输出不要混淆。
76	
77	#### 4.1.3 源码精读
78	
79	**① 唯一探测点。** [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2209-L2213](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2209-L2213)：`main()` 开头三行完成全部探测——`discover()`、把 `toolkit.nvcc` 转成所有权字符串、用 `header_dir("cuda.h")` 定头目录并在 `None` 时回落 `root.join("include")`。注意这里探测只发生一次；整个近三千行的构建脚本没有任何第二次 `discover()`。
80	
81	**② nvcc 命令的包装与分发。** nvcc 字符串不直接 `Command::new`，而是经 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L354-L364](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L354-L364) 的 `nvcc_command` 包装：设置了 `PEGAINFER_NVCC_LAUNCHER` 时用启动器前缀，否则直接 `Command::new(nvcc)`——裸 `"nvcc"` 的 `$PATH` 回落（u2-l3 讲过）正是在这里被 `Command` 解析。并行编译时每个 worker 线程克隆一份字符串：[pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2799-L2814](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2799-L2814)，线程从共享任务队列弹出 `NvccTask`、用 `nvcc_command(&nvcc)` 起进程。
82	
83	**③ nvcc 的 `-isystem`。** 每个 `.cu` 编译任务的公共前缀在 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2347-L2357](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2347-L2357)：`-isystem {cuda_include}` 加 CTK 头，`-I {csrc_dir}` 加项目源码头。为什么 CTK 用 `-isystem` 而不是 `-I`？[pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L35-L39](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L35-L39) 的注释给了答案：自带的 vendored CCCL 必须以 `-I` 传入，才能压过 `-isystem` 里工具包自带的旧版 CCCL——FlashInfer v0.6+ 需要旧 CTK 缺失的 API。哪些源文件需要 CCCL 由 stem 门控清单决定：[pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2497-L2507](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2497-L2507)（本次 HEAD 新增的 `dflash2_selector`、`qwen4_grouped_rmsnorm` 就加在这里）。
84	
85	**④ cuda_include 的宿主 cc 消费点。** 三处宿主编译都需要它：
86	
87	- glm52 cutedsl：feature 开启时 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2227-L2230](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2227-L2230) 调 `build_glm52_cutedsl_fp8_dsl(&crate_root(), &out_dir, &cuda_include)`；函数内 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L128-L132](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L128-L132) 用 `shim.include(cuda_include)` 编译 shim C 文件（其第 17 行 `#include <cuda_runtime.h>` 就是这个 `-I` 的服务对象）。
88	- qwen35 Triton AOT：[pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L1321-L1327](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L1321-L1327) 先断言 `cuda_include/cuda.h` 存在（panic 文案带 `set CUDA_HOME` 提示），再由 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L1503-L1508](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L1503-L1508) 的 `cc::Build` 编译生成的 C 包装。注释点明动机：宿主 cc 不像 nvcc 那样自己找得到 cuda.h。
89	- TileLang 生成体：三个调用点把 `&cuda_include` 传进 `tilelang_nvcc_tasks`，在 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2172-L2180](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2172-L2180) 变成 nvcc 的 `-I`。
90	
91	**⑤ root 与 kernel-lab。** 设置了 `PEGAINFER_KERNEL_LAB` 时，[pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2870-L2872](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2870-L2872) 把整个 `toolkit` 传给 `link_kernel_lab_shared`，后者在 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L941-L951](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L941-L951) 用 `toolkit.root.join("lib64")` 拼出 nvcc 链接器的 `-L` 参数并链接 `-lcudart -lcublas ...`。注意这是给**链接器进程**的参数，不是 cargo: 指令——同一个「库目录」概念在两种输出里各出现一次。
92	
93	**⑥ 尾部收口。** [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2882-L2899](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2882-L2899)：先为 `OUT_DIR`（静态库所在）发射 link-search；Windows 下绕过 `link_search()` 直接发射 `{root}/lib/x64`（Windows 工具包的库目录习惯与 Linux 不同），非 Windows 才调用 `toolkit.link_search()`；随后是一串 `cargo:rustc-link-lib`（`kernels_cuda` 静态库、`cudart`、`cublas`、`cublasLt`、`cuda`、`nvrtc`）。库名由消费方自己发射——`link_search` 只管目录（u2-l4 的契约）。L2895-2896 的注释还提醒：`libcuda.so` 在系统库目录而非工具包目录，靠链接器的默认搜索解析。
94

112	#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案
113	
114	**练习 1**：kernels 为什么从不直接遍历 `toolkit.include_dirs` 给编译器加 `-I`？
115	
116	<details><summary>参考答案</summary>
117	
118	因为 `include_dirs` 只保证「目录存在」，不保证「含所需的头」——conda 前缀的 `include/` 存在却缺 CUDA 头（[pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs:L123-L124](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs#L123-L124) 的文档注释明说了这一点）。kernels 只需要「真正含 cuda.h 的那一个」目录，`header_dir` 正是为此设计的单点查询。
119	</details>
120	
121	**练习 2**：`toolkit` 传进 `link_kernel_lab_shared` 后（L929），函数体里用了哪个出口？为什么不用 `link_search()`？
122	
123	<details><summary>参考答案</summary>
124	
125	只用了 `root`：在 L944 拼 `-L {root}/lib64` 传给 nvcc 链接器。不用 `link_search()` 是因为后者发射的是 `cargo:rustc-link-search` 指令（影响 rustc 最终链接 Rust crate），而 kernel-lab 是构建期由 nvcc 直接链接的独立 `.so`，需要的是链接器命令行参数——两者输出通道完全不同。
126	</details>
127	
128	**练习 3**：`nvcc` 出口在 kernels 里经过了几层间接才真正变成进程？
129	
130	<details><summary>参考答案</summary>
131	
132	三层：L2210 把 `PathBuf` 转成字符串 → 各编译任务把它克隆进 worker 线程（L2803）→ `nvcc_command(&nvcc)` 包装（可选的 `PEGAINFER_NVCC_LAUNCHER` 前缀）后 `Command` 起进程。裸 `"nvcc"` 回落时，`$PATH` 解析发生在 `Command` 执行那一刻。
133	</details>
134	
135	### 4.2 cupti 的 extras/CUPTI 目录特例
136	
137	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
138	
139	CUPTI 的头文件与库在经典安装里位于 `extras/CUPTI/include` 与 `extras/CUPTI/lib64`，**不在**主 `include/`、`lib64/` 里。回看 u2-l3：`from_root` 的候选目录只覆盖 `include`、`lib64/lib`、`targets/<arch>` 和 HPC SDK 的 `math_libs` 兄弟树（[pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs:L91-L121](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs#L91-L121)），完全不认识 `extras` 子树。
140	
141	这是有意的 API 边界：`pegainfer-build` 保持「通用 CUDA 工具包探测」，具体组件的安装特例交给消费方用 `root` 自己拼。`pegainfer-cupti/build.rs` 就是这种分工的教科书示例——34 行走完 discover → include → compile → link 全流程，外加一个组件级特例。
142	
143	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
144	
145	```text
146	toolkit = CudaToolkit::discover()                        # L5
147	cupti_include = root/extras/CUPTI/include                # L7
148	cupti_lib64   = root/extras/CUPTI/lib64                  # L8
149	
150	cc::Build（宿主编译 range_profiler.cpp）：
151	  .includes(&toolkit.include_dirs)                       # L16，主工具包头（直接用字段！）
152	  if cupti_include.is_dir() { .include(cupti_include) }  # L17-19，特例头，软门控
153	  .compile("pegainfer_cupti_range_profiler")             # L20
154	
155	toolkit.link_search()                                    # L22，主库目录
156	if cupti_lib64.is_dir() { cargo:rustc-link-search=... }  # L23-25，特例库，软门控

212	### 4.3 CudaToolkit 四个出口（root/nvcc/include_dirs/lib_dirs）的用途映射
213	
214	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
215	
216	u1-l3 介绍过结构体的可见性设计：`root`、`nvcc`、`include_dirs` 公开，`lib_dirs` 私有、唯一出口是 `link_search()`。本模块把两个真实消费方的用法叠上去，得到这张完整的「出口 → 用途」映射表——它同时是二次开发时的选型指南：**新写一个 build.rs 时，每个需求该走哪个出口？**
217	
218	- 要起编译器/链接器进程 → `nvcc`；
219	- 要按具体头文件定位目录 → `header_dir("某头文件")`（`include_dirs` 的推荐消费方式）；
220	- 要给宿主 cc 一批宽松的候选目录 → 直接 `include_dirs`；
221	- 要组件特例路径 → `root` 自己拼；
222	- 要 rustc 链接搜索 → `link_search()`，别自己碰库目录。
223	
224	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
225	
226	| 出口 | 可见性 | kernels 的消费点（HEAD 8886aa47） | cupti 的消费点 | 最终形态 |
227	|---|---|---|---|---|
228	| `root` | pub | 兜底 `root/include`（L2213）；kernel-lab `-L root/lib64`（L944）；Windows `root/lib/x64`（L2885-2887） | `extras/CUPTI/{include,lib64}`（L7-8） | 编译器 argv 或 cargo: 指令 |
229	| `nvcc` | pub | L2210 → `nvcc_command`（L354-364）→ 并行 worker（L2803） | 不用 | 子进程 argv |
230	| `include_dirs` | pub | 不直接用；经 `header_dir("cuda.h")` 单点消费（L2211-2212） | 直接遍历 `.includes()`（L16） | `-I` / `-isystem` |
231	| `lib_dirs` | 私有 | 仅 `link_search()`（L2889，非 Windows） | 仅 `link_search()`（L22） | `cargo:rustc-link-search=native=...` |
232	
233	两个消费方恰好示范了 `include_dirs` 的两种消费姿势：kernels 是「精确制导」（只信 `header_dir` 的单点结果），cupti 是「面多加水」（候选全给，编译器自己挑）。前者服务于「头文件版本敏感」的场景，后者适合「有就行」的包装层。

327	**待本地验证**：数据流图的行号来自本讲已核对的 grep 与阅读；请在本地重跑步骤 1 的 grep 复核。若本地有 GPU + CUDA 环境，可再跑一次 `cargo build --release -p pegainfer-kernels` 观察构建日志里的 `cargo:warning=Compiling CUDA kernels for nvcc targets: ...`（无环境时跳过，不影响结论）。
328	
329	## 6. 本讲小结
330	
331	- kernels 全文件只有**一个**探测点（L2209-2213）：`discover()` 之后立即派生出 `nvcc` 字符串与 `cuda_include`（`header_dir("cuda.h")` + `root/include` 兜底），其余近三千行都在消费这两个派生物和 `root`。
332	- `CudaToolkit` 的出口一半喂**编译器 argv**（nvcc、cuda_include、kernel-lab 的 `-L`），一半喂 **cargo: 指令**（`link_search` 的 `rustc-link-search`）；同一个「库目录」概念在两种通道里各出现一次，别混淆。
333	- kernels 不直接遍历 `include_dirs`，只信 `header_dir` 的单点结果（conda 的 `include/` 存在却缺头）；cupti 则直接 `.includes(&toolkit.include_dirs)` 给宿主 cc——两种姿势对应「版本敏感」与「有就行」两类场景。
334	- cupti 用公开的 `root` 拼 `extras/CUPTI/{include,lib64}` 组件特例目录，并用两个 `is_dir()` 软门控优雅降级；组件级布局特例放消费方、通用工具包布局放库，是这条 API 边界的分工原则。
335	- `header_dir` 返回 `None` 时的 `root.join("include")` 兜底在 conda 布局下不可靠：指向一个「存在但没有 CUDA 头」的目录，把清晰的探测失败变成含糊的编译错误；Triton AOT 路径的 `assert!` + hint 是更稳的范式。
336	- 本次 HEAD 更新（223206b7→8886aa47）只给 kernels 的 CCCL `-I` 门控清单加了两个 stem 并改写一句警告，L2500 以下行号整体 +2；工具包消费点中仅尾部 link_search 从 2884-2887 漂移到 2886-2889。
337	
338	## 7. 下一步学习建议
339	
340	- **下一讲 u3-l3（rerun-if 语义与构建缓存正确性）**：本讲反复出现 `rerun-if-env-changed`（藏在 `discover()` 里）与 `rerun-if-changed`（cupti L33、cutedsl L125-127），下一讲系统拆解 Cargo 指纹机制——「换了 CUDA 安装但环境变量没变」时构建缓存为什么可能过期、怎么规避。

# 消费方集成：kernels 与 cupti 如何使用 CudaToolkit

## 1. 本讲目标

前几讲我们一直在读 `pegainfer-build` 这个库本身：discover 的回落链、target_dirs 的架构目录、from_root 的三种布局、existing_deduped 的收敛、header_dir 与 link_search 的输出。本讲换到**消费方视角**，回答一个新问题：**一个真实的 build.rs 拿到 `CudaToolkit` 之后，到底怎么用它的各个出口？**

学完本讲你应该能够：

1. 在 `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` 近三千行代码中定位**全部**工具包使用点，并逐个说明用途。
2. 说清 `header_dir("cuda.h")` 返回 `None` 时 kernels 的兜底路径（`toolkit.root.join("include")`），以及这个兜底在 conda 布局下为什么不可靠。
3. 对比两个消费方的使用深度：kernels 用 nvcc / header_dir / link_search / root 四个出口，而 cupti 不用 nvcc、却额外用 `root` 拼 `extras/CUPTI` 特例目录。
4. 独立画出「discover 输出 → 各消费点用途 → 最终 cargo: 指令（或编译器 argv）」的完整数据流图。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲假设你已完成 u1（build script 协议、lib.rs 导览）和 u2（探测机制精读）。在此之上补充四个新概念：

- **宿主编译器 vs nvcc**：nvcc 编译 `.cu` 时自己知道 CUDA 工具包（CTK）的头文件在哪；但宿主机的 `cc` / `c++` 编译一个 `#include <cuda_runtime.h>` 的 C 包装文件时**不会**自动找到 CUDA 头，必须显式传 `-I`。这是 `header_dir` 存在的根本原因——它要回答「哪一个目录里**真的**有这个头文件」。
- **`-I` 与 `-isystem` 的区别**：两者都添加头文件搜索目录，但 `-isystem` 把目录标记为「系统头」（抑制其中警告），且优先级低于 `-I`。kernels 正是利用这个优先级差，把 CTK 头目录装进 `-isystem`、把自带的较新 CCCL 装进 `-I`，让后者覆盖前者。
- **cc crate**：Rust 生态驱动宿主 C/C++ 编译器的标准 build-dependency；`cc::Build::include(path)` 等价于给编译器加 `-I path`。
- **CUPTI**（CUDA Profiling Tools Interface）：CUDA 的性能剖析接口。它的头和库在经典安装里**不在**主 `include/`、`lib64/` 下，而在 `extras/CUPTI/` 子树——这是本讲第二个模块的主角。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 体量 | 本讲角色 |
|---|---|---|
| `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` | 约 2930 行 | 构建总管：编译全部 CUDA 源、Triton AOT、TileLang、cutedsl，是 `CudaToolkit` 最重的消费方 |
| `pegainfer-cupti/build.rs` | 34 行 | 最小完整消费方：discover → include → compile → link 一条龙，外加 extras/CUPTI 特例 |
| `pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs` | 299 行 | 被消费的库本尊（u1-l3、u2 各讲已精读，本讲只引用关键行） |
| `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/glm52/glm52_fp8_dsl_gemm.c` | — | cutedsl shim 源文件，用来验证兜底风险（只看第 17 行的 `#include`） |

两个消费方在各自 `Cargo.toml` 的 `[build-dependencies]` 里以 workspace 依赖声明引用本库：[pegainfer-cupti/Cargo.toml:L7-L9](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/Cargo.toml#L7-L9)（`cc` + `pegainfer-build`）与 [pegainfer-kernels/Cargo.toml:L27-L29](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/Cargo.toml#L27-L29)（同样两条）。

> **行号校准记录（update）**：上一版讲义以 223206b7 为基准。当前 HEAD 8886aa47 期间，73d998ea（Qwen4 分组 RMSNorm）与 8b5b84a9（DFlash2）触碰了 kernels，但 `build.rs` 只有 4 行改动：往 CCCL `-I` 门控清单加了两个 stem（[L2500](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2500) 的 `dflash2_selector`、[L2504](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2504) 的 `qwen4_grouped_rmsnorm`）并改写了一句 Qwen4 警告文案（[L2739](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2739)）。这使 L2500 以下行号整体 +2：尾部工具包出口从旧版的 2884-2887 漂移到 2886-2889；而 L929、L2209-2213 等锚点不变。`pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs` 与 `pegainfer-cupti/build.rs` 两个文件无任何改动。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 kernels 构建链路中的工具包消费点

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`pegainfer-kernels` 是整个工作区的构建总管：`csrc/*.cu` 的 nvcc 编译、qwen35 的 Triton AOT、glm52 的 TileLang 与 cutedsl 代码生成、静态库打包、kernel-lab 共享库链接，全部从这里发起。它对 `CudaToolkit` 的需求最全面：

- 要一个**可执行的 nvcc 命令**（几十个并行编译任务都要用它）；
- 要一个**真正含 `cuda.h` 的头目录**，同时喂给 nvcc（`-isystem`）和宿主 cc（`-I`）；
- 要**库搜索路径**，在构建末尾变成 `cargo:rustc-link-search`。

值得注意的是：kernels **从不直接遍历 `toolkit.include_dirs`**——它只消费 `header_dir("cuda.h")` 的单点结果。原因在 u2-l4 讲过：`include_dirs` 里可能有「存在却缺 CUDA 头」的目录（conda 前缀的 `include/`），只有按具体头文件探测才可靠。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

kernels 的 `main()` 在开头一次性完成探测，之后所有消费点都用这三样派生物：

```text
toolkit = CudaToolkit::discover()                    # L2209，全文件唯一探测点
nvcc         = toolkit.nvcc（转成字符串）             # L2210 → nvcc_command 包装 → 并行 worker 克隆
cuda_include = header_dir("cuda.h")                  # L2211-2212
               ?? toolkit.root.join("include")       # L2213，兜底（见 4.3.4）

cuda_include 的四条下游：
  ├─ nvcc 编译 .cu        ：-isystem {cuda_include}          # L2353-2354
  ├─ glm52 cutedsl shim   ：宿主 cc -I                      # L2229 → L129
  ├─ qwen35 Triton AOT    ：断言 + 宿主 cc -I                # L2875 → L1323-1327 / L1506
  └─ TileLang 生成体      ：nvcc -I                          # L2748/2757/2771 → L2178-2179

toolkit.root 的两条下游：
  ├─ kernel-lab .so 链接  ：-L {root}/lib64（仅 PEGAINFER_KERNEL_LAB）# L2871 → L944
  └─ Windows 库目录       ：cargo:rustc-link-search={root}/lib/x64    # L2883-2887

lib_dirs 的唯一下游：
  └─ toolkit.link_search()（非 Windows）                    # L2889
       → cargo:rustc-link-search=native=... 配合 L2891-2899 的 link-lib 清单
```

关键认知：`nvcc` 和 `cuda_include` 变成**子进程 argv**，`link_search` 变成 **cargo: 指令**——`CudaToolkit` 的出口一半喂编译器、一半喂 Cargo，两类输出不要混淆。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**① 唯一探测点。** [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2209-L2213](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2209-L2213)：`main()` 开头三行完成全部探测——`discover()`、把 `toolkit.nvcc` 转成所有权字符串、用 `header_dir("cuda.h")` 定头目录并在 `None` 时回落 `root.join("include")`。注意这里探测只发生一次；整个近三千行的构建脚本没有任何第二次 `discover()`。

**② nvcc 命令的包装与分发。** nvcc 字符串不直接 `Command::new`，而是经 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L354-L364](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L354-L364) 的 `nvcc_command` 包装：设置了 `PEGAINFER_NVCC_LAUNCHER` 时用启动器前缀，否则直接 `Command::new(nvcc)`——裸 `"nvcc"` 的 `$PATH` 回落（u2-l3 讲过）正是在这里被 `Command` 解析。并行编译时每个 worker 线程克隆一份字符串：[pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2799-L2814](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2799-L2814)，线程从共享任务队列弹出 `NvccTask`、用 `nvcc_command(&nvcc)` 起进程。

**③ nvcc 的 `-isystem`。** 每个 `.cu` 编译任务的公共前缀在 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2347-L2357](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2347-L2357)：`-isystem {cuda_include}` 加 CTK 头，`-I {csrc_dir}` 加项目源码头。为什么 CTK 用 `-isystem` 而不是 `-I`？[pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L35-L39](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L35-L39) 的注释给了答案：自带的 vendored CCCL 必须以 `-I` 传入，才能压过 `-isystem` 里工具包自带的旧版 CCCL——FlashInfer v0.6+ 需要旧 CTK 缺失的 API。哪些源文件需要 CCCL 由 stem 门控清单决定：[pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2497-L2507](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2497-L2507)（本次 HEAD 新增的 `dflash2_selector`、`qwen4_grouped_rmsnorm` 就加在这里）。

**④ cuda_include 的宿主 cc 消费点。** 三处宿主编译都需要它：

- glm52 cutedsl：feature 开启时 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2227-L2230](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2227-L2230) 调 `build_glm52_cutedsl_fp8_dsl(&crate_root(), &out_dir, &cuda_include)`；函数内 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L128-L132](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L128-L132) 用 `shim.include(cuda_include)` 编译 shim C 文件（其第 17 行 `#include <cuda_runtime.h>` 就是这个 `-I` 的服务对象）。
- qwen35 Triton AOT：[pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L1321-L1327](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L1321-L1327) 先断言 `cuda_include/cuda.h` 存在（panic 文案带 `set CUDA_HOME` 提示），再由 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L1503-L1508](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L1503-L1508) 的 `cc::Build` 编译生成的 C 包装。注释点明动机：宿主 cc 不像 nvcc 那样自己找得到 cuda.h。
- TileLang 生成体：三个调用点把 `&cuda_include` 传进 `tilelang_nvcc_tasks`，在 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2172-L2180](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2172-L2180) 变成 nvcc 的 `-I`。

**⑤ root 与 kernel-lab。** 设置了 `PEGAINFER_KERNEL_LAB` 时，[pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2870-L2872](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2870-L2872) 把整个 `toolkit` 传给 `link_kernel_lab_shared`，后者在 [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L941-L951](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L941-L951) 用 `toolkit.root.join("lib64")` 拼出 nvcc 链接器的 `-L` 参数并链接 `-lcudart -lcublas ...`。注意这是给**链接器进程**的参数，不是 cargo: 指令——同一个「库目录」概念在两种输出里各出现一次。

**⑥ 尾部收口。** [pegainfer-kernels/build.rs:L2882-L2899](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-kernels/build.rs#L2882-L2899)：先为 `OUT_DIR`（静态库所在）发射 link-search；Windows 下绕过 `link_search()` 直接发射 `{root}/lib/x64`（Windows 工具包的库目录习惯与 Linux 不同），非 Windows 才调用 `toolkit.link_search()`；随后是一串 `cargo:rustc-link-lib`（`kernels_cuda` 静态库、`cudart`、`cublas`、`cublasLt`、`cuda`、`nvrtc`）。库名由消费方自己发射——`link_search` 只管目录（u2-l4 的契约）。L2895-2896 的注释还提醒：`libcuda.so` 在系统库目录而非工具包目录，靠链接器的默认搜索解析。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：不借助本讲义，独立复现「全部工具包使用点」清单，验证与 4.1.2 的数据流一致。

**操作步骤**：

1. 在仓库根目录执行 `grep -n "toolkit\|header_dir\|link_search" pegainfer-kernels/build.rs`；
2. 对每条命中分类：是真代码、注释还是 panic 文案里的英文单词（例如 L1325 的命中只是报错信息里的 "toolkit" 一词）；
3. 再执行 `grep -n "cuda_include" pegainfer-kernels/build.rs`，把 `cuda_include` 的每处出现挂到 4.1.2 数据流的对应分支上；
4. 用 `git log --oneline -3 -- pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` 确认本讲校准记录里提到的最近提交。

**需要观察的现象**：`toolkit` 的真实代码命中应恰好是 L929（函数参数）、L944（root/lib64）、L2209-2213（探测三连）、L2871（传参）、L2886（Windows 分支）、L2889（link_search）；`cuda_include` 的出现全部能追溯到 L2211 这一个定义点。

**预期结果**：你手绘的数据流图与 4.1.2 一致；多余的命中都被你正确识别为注释或文案。

**待本地验证**：本实践是纯源码阅读，无需 GPU、无需 CUDA，任何机器可做；grep 输出请在本地实际运行确认。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：kernels 为什么从不直接遍历 `toolkit.include_dirs` 给编译器加 `-I`？

<details><summary>参考答案</summary>

因为 `include_dirs` 只保证「目录存在」，不保证「含所需的头」——conda 前缀的 `include/` 存在却缺 CUDA 头（[pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs:L123-L124](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs#L123-L124) 的文档注释明说了这一点）。kernels 只需要「真正含 cuda.h 的那一个」目录，`header_dir` 正是为此设计的单点查询。
</details>

**练习 2**：`toolkit` 传进 `link_kernel_lab_shared` 后（L929），函数体里用了哪个出口？为什么不用 `link_search()`？

<details><summary>参考答案</summary>

### 4.2 cupti 的 extras/CUPTI 目录特例

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

CUPTI 的头文件与库在经典安装里位于 `extras/CUPTI/include` 与 `extras/CUPTI/lib64`，**不在**主 `include/`、`lib64/` 里。回看 u2-l3：`from_root` 的候选目录只覆盖 `include`、`lib64/lib`、`targets/<arch>` 和 HPC SDK 的 `math_libs` 兄弟树（[pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs:L91-L121](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs#L91-L121)），完全不认识 `extras` 子树。

这是有意的 API 边界：`pegainfer-build` 保持「通用 CUDA 工具包探测」，具体组件的安装特例交给消费方用 `root` 自己拼。`pegainfer-cupti/build.rs` 就是这种分工的教科书示例——34 行走完 discover → include → compile → link 全流程，外加一个组件级特例。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
toolkit = CudaToolkit::discover()                        # L5
cupti_include = root/extras/CUPTI/include                # L7
cupti_lib64   = root/extras/CUPTI/lib64                  # L8

cc::Build（宿主编译 range_profiler.cpp）：
  .includes(&toolkit.include_dirs)                       # L16，主工具包头（直接用字段！）
  if cupti_include.is_dir() { .include(cupti_include) }  # L17-19，特例头，软门控
  .compile("pegainfer_cupti_range_profiler")             # L20

toolkit.link_search()                                    # L22，主库目录
if cupti_lib64.is_dir() { cargo:rustc-link-search=... }  # L23-25，特例库，软门控
cargo:rustc-link-lib = cuda / cupti / stdc++(非Windows)  # L27-31
cargo:rerun-if-changed=csrc/range_profiler.cpp           # L33
```

「软门控」是本模块的关键词：两个 `is_dir()` 判断让没有 `extras/CUPTI` 的安装（比如 conda 布局）不至于在构建期立刻炸掉，而是优雅降级——目录不存在就跳过这条额外路径。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**① discover 与特例路径的拼装。** [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L4-L8](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L4-L8)：一行 `discover()` 之后，立刻用**公开字段 `root`** 拼出 `extras/CUPTI/include` 与 `extras/CUPTI/lib64` 两个路径。注释直言：「CUPTI 在经典安装里位于主工具包目录之外」。

**② 编译期：include_dirs 的直接消费。** [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L10-L20](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L10-L20)：与 kernels 不同，cupti **直接遍历** `toolkit.include_dirs` 整个字段（`.includes()` 复数形式），因为它编译的 C++ 文件要同时用主工具包头和 CUPTI 头，多给几个候选目录无害；`is_dir()` 命中时再补 CUPTI 特例头目录，最后 `compile()`。

**③ 链接期：link_search 与特例库。** [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L22-L31](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L22-L31)：先 `toolkit.link_search()` 输出主库目录，再为 `extras/CUPTI/lib64` 补一条手写的 `cargo:rustc-link-search=native=...`（注意格式要自己写全，因为这条不经库的 `link_search`）；随后三条 `cargo:rustc-link-lib`——`cuda`、`cupti`，以及仅在非 Windows 上的 `stdc++`（CUPTI 头引用的 C++ 运行时符号在 Linux 上由 libstdc++ 提供，MSVC 工具链自带）。

**④ 缓存契约。** [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L33](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L33)：`rerun-if-changed` 盯住唯一源文件。注意 `CUDA_HOME`/`CUDA_PATH` 的 rerun-if 声明藏在库的 `discover()` 里（u2-l1、u3-l3 展开），消费方不必重复。

### 4.3 CudaToolkit 四个出口（root/nvcc/include_dirs/lib_dirs）的用途映射

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

u1-l3 介绍过结构体的可见性设计：`root`、`nvcc`、`include_dirs` 公开，`lib_dirs` 私有、唯一出口是 `link_search()`。本模块把两个真实消费方的用法叠上去，得到这张完整的「出口 → 用途」映射表——它同时是二次开发时的选型指南：**新写一个 build.rs 时，每个需求该走哪个出口？**

- 要起编译器/链接器进程 → `nvcc`；
- 要按具体头文件定位目录 → `header_dir("某头文件")`（`include_dirs` 的推荐消费方式）；
- 要给宿主 cc 一批宽松的候选目录 → 直接 `include_dirs`；
- 要组件特例路径 → `root` 自己拼；
- 要 rustc 链接搜索 → `link_search()`，别自己碰库目录。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

| 出口 | 可见性 | kernels 的消费点（HEAD 8886aa47） | cupti 的消费点 | 最终形态 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `root` | pub | 兜底 `root/include`（L2213）；kernel-lab `-L root/lib64`（L944）；Windows `root/lib/x64`（L2885-2887） | `extras/CUPTI/{include,lib64}`（L7-8） | 编译器 argv 或 cargo: 指令 |
| `nvcc` | pub | L2210 → `nvcc_command`（L354-364）→ 并行 worker（L2803） | 不用 | 子进程 argv |
| `include_dirs` | pub | 不直接用；经 `header_dir("cuda.h")` 单点消费（L2211-2212） | 直接遍历 `.includes()`（L16） | `-I` / `-isystem` |
| `lib_dirs` | 私有 | 仅 `link_search()`（L2889，非 Windows） | 仅 `link_search()`（L22） | `cargo:rustc-link-search=native=...` |

两个消费方恰好示范了 `include_dirs` 的两种消费姿势：kernels 是「精确制导」（只信 `header_dir` 的单点结果），cupti 是「面多加水」（候选全给，编译器自己挑）。前者服务于「头文件版本敏感」的场景，后者适合「有就行」的包装层。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**① 出口的定义处。** [pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs:L67-L73](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs#L67-L73)：结构体四个字段，`nvcc` 的文档注释写明回落语义（`{root}/bin/nvcc` 存在则用之，否则裸 `nvcc` 走 `$PATH`）。

**② header_dir 与 link_search 的契约。** [pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs:L123-L130](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs#L123-L130) 是 `header_dir`：按头文件逐目录探测，返回 `Option`——**None 是合法返回**，怎么处理是消费方的责任（kernels 的兜底见 4.3.4）。[pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs:L132-L142](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs#L132-L142) 是 `link_search`：空表软告警，非空逐目录发射 `native=` 指令。

**③ None 场景的库内锚点。** [pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs:L260-L269](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs#L260-L269) 的 `unknown_layout_yields_nothing` 测试：探测一个只有 `weird/place` 的根目录，断言 `header_dir("cuda.h")` 返回 `None`、两个目录列表全空——这正是触发 kernels 兜底的场景在库侧的样子。
